chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Lafayette vaudeville shows and meeting his wife in the chorus line
summary: Crawford recalls playing for acts and a chorus line at the Lafayette and meeting his wife, a chorus girl, on the road with the band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: our way. After the Cotton Club, Lafayette, Cotton Club, we were on our way.
Now, how -- what kind of shows were you playing at the Lafayette?
Played a little vaudeville, you know, Dusty Best of Fletcher, acts and a chorus line. I met my wife -- my wife was a chorus girl.
Well Anyway Alone, I met you as a chorus girl.
You met your wife on the Harlem Express. She says you met her --
As a chorus girl, but now --
She was on the road with -- in the line with Lunsford's band, Harlem Express.
Now, when you were playing the shows, now, you have -- did you have to play -- the band played for -- they played for meetings and dances?
Yeah, Dusty Best of Fletcher, Ables and Esther [Lieder] oh, just I played in many acts.
Well, did -- how did you like doing that part of it? Did you like that part of the show?
Yeah, it was a challenge, so I did it
